Title: Access not removed within SLA for 3 of 10 sampled leavers
Criteria (requirement): Access Control Policy v1.0 s5.3: access removed within 1 business day of termination.
Condition observed: Of 10 sampled leavers (population 34), 7 had accounts disabled within 1 business day. Two were disabled after 2 and 10 business days, and one account was still active at the test date (2026-10-12).
Potential risk / impact: Former employees could retain access to business systems. No evidence reviewed shows the accounts were used after termination; activity logs were not reviewed in this assessment.
Root cause: Under investigation. Initial observation: HR notifies IT by email with no ticket or tracking.
Recommendation: Disable the remaining account immediately. Link HR termination ticket to an IT task with the SLA. Reconcile HR leaver list to active accounts weekly. Review activity logs for the 3 accounts.

Title: No evidence of backup restoration testing in 2026
Criteria (requirement): Backup Procedure v1.1: restoration test of critical systems at least every six months.
Condition observed: No restoration test records for 2026 were provided. Backup job reports show jobs completing (EV-007) but do not demonstrate recoverability.
Potential risk / impact: The company may be unable to restore critical data within the time needed after an incident. This finding does not state that backups are unrecoverable; recoverability is unverified.
Root cause: Under investigation. No owner appears to be assigned to schedule tests.
Recommendation: Perform and document a restoration test for the order and finance databases. Add tests to a compliance calendar with an evidence template.

Title: Q3 privileged access review lacks sign-off and documented outcomes
Criteria (requirement): Access Control Policy s6.2: quarterly review with reviewer sign-off and exceptions resolved.
Condition observed: The Q3 review record shows an account list exported 2026-09-12 with 4 accounts marked 'to review'. No reviewer sign-off or outcome for these 4 accounts was provided.
Potential risk / impact: Unnecessary privileged access may persist. The extent is unknown until outcomes are documented.
Root cause: Under investigation. Procedure has no sign-off step or reminder.
Recommendation: Document outcomes for the 4 accounts. Add a sign-off step and reminder workflow.

Title: Payroll vendor approved after contract start; data feed not minimised
Criteria (requirement): Vendor Risk Procedure: due diligence and approval before contract signature; collect only necessary data.
Condition observed: PayrollPro contract was signed 2026-03-02; assessment and approval are dated 2026-04-20. The payroll export includes performance-rating and medical-leave fields that the vendor data-flow diagram shows are not needed for payroll. The DPA excerpt has no vendor breach-notification timeframe.
Potential risk / impact: More employee personal information is exposed if the vendor is compromised. BrightCart's own incident obligations may be harder to meet.
Root cause: To be confirmed. Procurement may be able to sign contracts without a GRC approval gate.
Recommendation: Remove unneeded fields from the feed. Add a breach-notification timeframe to the DPA (Legal to advise on applicable requirements). Add an approval gate before contract signature.

Title: Incident reporting procedure does not define a reporting timeframe
Criteria (requirement): Security Policy s8: suspected incidents must be reported promptly.
Condition observed: Procedure v1.0 does not define 'promptly', and does not name an out-of-hours contact.
Potential risk / impact: Delayed reporting could delay response and any required notifications. Actual reporting delays were not tested.
Recommendation: Define a timeframe and out-of-hours contact in procedure v2.0, then brief all staff. Test operation in the next cycle.

Title: Security awareness training completion below target
Criteria (requirement): Security Awareness Standard: at least 95% of staff complete annual training by 30 Sep.
Condition observed: At 2026-09-30, 126 of 150 employees (84%) had completed training.
Potential risk / impact: Untrained staff may be more likely to fall for phishing.
Root cause: Under investigation. Reminders may not be escalated to managers.
Recommendation: Send reminders and escalate to managers; report completion monthly until 95% is reached.
